title: Beginners Bellydance Tutorial | By Leilah Isaac

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Leilah guides beginners through gentle full-body warmups with detailed postural alignment and continuous encouragement. She breaks down isolation movements step-by-step, focusing on flexibility and muscle conditioning.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction to the beginners belly dance workout and channel info
Explanation of basic posture, feet alignment, pelvis neutral position, and upper body stance
Full-body stretching warm-up with arm reaches and plie squat variations
Detailed breakdown of side, back, and forward hip stretches and isolations
Slower practice of upper body stretches and side-to-side rib isolation
Instruction on hip shifting outside normal body alignment
Leg lifts, ankle circles, and toe points for strengthening

metaphors: Imagine river flowing from your hands
Pelvis has a mind of the road
common_mistakes: Bending forward instead of keeping posture
Arching pelvis too far under or back
Slanted side-to-side movement instead of pulling
safety: Do not worry how far you can go today, your body will improve

steps_taught.name: Basic Posture
steps_taught.description: Feet under hips, knees slightly bent, pelvis in mid neutral position, shoulders back, chest lifted.

steps_taught.name: Plie Stretch Warmup
steps_taught.description: In and release plie with arms crossing and extending overhead.

steps_taught.name: Hip Side Stretch
steps_taught.description: Squeezing and pushing hip to one side with knees bent for glute stretch.

steps_taught.name: Hip Shifts
steps_taught.description: Shifting hips side to side outside regular alignment with chest still.

what_works: Clear verbal explanations of posture and body mechanics
Repetitive practice from multiple angles including mirror
what_hinders: Long verbal explanations during static holding positions

quotes.text: So what we're going to be doing is doing a bit of a stretch kind of workout.
Once you find that mid-neutral position, that is your starting point for most moves.
I really want you to squeeze that hip, push it to one side.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher stands facing front in a room with a large mirror, gesturing while speaking.
Teacher demonstrates knee bend and pelvis alignment adjustment.
Teacher performs plie squats with arm extensions.
Teacher isolates hip push to the side with bent knees.

extraction.distinctive_method: Extensive use of visualization (e.g., river flowing from hands, pelvis having a mind of the road) paired with physical isolation holds.
